newsitem.title: USA: Court reverses ruling against Lloyd's underwriters.
newsitem.headline: Court reverses ruling against Lloyd's underwriters.

text.p: A U.S. District Court of Appeals has reversed a $70 million judgment against certain Lloyd's of London underwriters in an environmental cleanup dispute.

According to the law firm representing Lloyd's underwriters, the U.S. District Court of Appeals for the Third Circuit ruled that the London insurers are entitled to receive a credit against the judgement.

The appeals court decided the London insurers are not responsible for the entire judgement and that the case should be reviewed to calculate the amount they are responsible for, said Larry Eaton, a managing partner with Blatt, Hammesfahr & Eaton, the law firm representing Lloyd's underwriters.
Eaton said the London insurers' share of the liability could be as little as 10 percent or less of the judgement.
"We anticipate that the amount of previous judgment against the London insurers will be significantly reduced," Eaton stated.
The case, Koppers vs Aetna, was filed in September 1985 and involved insurance coverage for environmental pollution claims by Koppers Co Inc of Pittsburgh, Pennsyvania.
